name: Tomato
symptoms: Dark brown to black concentric rings on lower leaves, resembling a bullseye. Yellowing halos around spots, stem lesions, and fruit rot near the stem end.
causes: Fungal pathogen (Alternaria solani), favored by warm temperatures (24-29°C) and alternating wet and dry weather with high humidity.
organic_remedies: Spray Neem oil (5ml/L) or Trichoderma viride (10g/L). Remove and bury infected bottom leaves. Apply copper oxychloride bio-formulation.
chemical_remedies: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1ml/L at 10-day intervals.
precautions: Practice 3-year crop rotation; avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; maintain 60cm plant spacing for adequate airflow; stake plants to keep leaves off soil.
suggestions: Apply organic mulch (straw/plastic) to prevent soil splash during rain. Monitor lower foliage weekly.
soil_type: Well-drained sandy loam or clay loam, pH 6.0 - 6.8
fertilizer: Apply FYM 25 t/ha at field prep. Basal: 50% N, 100% P & K. Top-dress remaining 50% N in two splits at 30 and 50 days after transplanting.

name: Rice (Paddy)
symptoms: Spindle-shaped elliptical spots with grey/white centers and reddish-brown borders on leaves. Blackening of panicle node causing neck blast and chaffy grains.
causes: Fungus Magnaporthe oryzae (Pyricularia oryzae), triggered by cloudy humid weather, excess nitrogen fertilizer, and night temperatures around 20°C.
organic_remedies: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10g/kg seed. Spray 5% neem seed kernel extract (NSKE) at early spotting.
chemical_remedies: Foliar spray of Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g/L or Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5ml/L or Kasugamycin 3% SL @ 2ml/L.
precautions: Avoid heavy single doses of urea. Maintain proper field water level (don't let soil crack). Use blast-resistant seed varieties like MTU-1010, BPT-5204 (tolerant).
suggestions: Destroy previous crop stubbles. Apply silica fertilizer to strengthen plant cell walls against fungal penetration.
soil_type: Clayey or loamy fertile soil capable of holding water, pH 5.5 - 7.0
fertilizer: Basal: 50% N, full P, 50% K. Top-dress remaining 50% N in two equal splits at active tillering and panicle initiation along with 50% K.

name: Cotton
disease_te: గులాబీ రంగు కాయ తొలుచు పురుగు & నల్ల మచ్చ తెగులు
symptoms: Rosetted flowers, premature boll opening, damaged lint with staining, angular water-soaked dark brown spots on leaves turning into blackarm on branches.
causes: Pectinophora gossypiella larvae burrowing into squares/bolls; Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum bacteria under warm humid conditions.
organic_remedies: Install 8-10 pheromone traps per acre for monitoring. Release Trichogramma egg parasitoids @ 60,000/acre. Spray 5% NSKE or Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt).
chemical_remedies: Spray Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.5g/L or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3ml/L. For bacterial blight, spray Copper Oxychloride 3g/L + Streptocycline 0.1g/L.
precautions: Strictly follow non-Bt refuge planting; destroy crop residues immediately after harvest; avoid extending crop duration beyond 150 days.
suggestions: Monitor weekly using pheromone traps. Inspect 20 bolls per acre randomly for entry holes.
soil_type: Deep black cotton soils (Vertisols) or well-drained red sandy loams, pH 6.5 - 8.0
fertilizer: Basal: 25% N, 100% P, 50% K. Remaining N in 3 equal splits at squaring, peak flowering, and boll development.

name: Chilli
disease_te: ఆకు ముడుత మరియు కొమ్మ ఎండు తెగులు
symptoms: Upward and downward curling of leaves with reduced leaf size; necrosis of tips drying downwards (dieback), circular sunken black spots on ripe fruits.
causes: Leaf curl virus transmitted by whiteflies and thrips; Anthracnose caused by Colletotrichum capsici under warm, humid conditions.
organic_remedies: Install yellow and blue sticky traps (15/acre). Spray Dashaparni extract or Fish amino acid. Spray Neem oil (10,000 ppm) @ 2ml/L.
chemical_remedies: To control vector thrips/whiteflies: Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.25g/L or Fipronil 5% SC @ 2ml/L. For Anthracnose: Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1ml/L.
precautions: Use barrier crops (2 rows of maize/sorghum around chilli field); avoid excess nitrogen; remove and burn severely infested virus plants.
suggestions: Maintain clean field bunds. Ensure balanced zinc and boron micronutrient sprays at flowering.
soil_type: Well-drained light loamy or black soils, pH 6.5 - 7.5
fertilizer: Apply farmyard manure 25 t/ha. Apply P basal, N & K in 4 split doses (transplanting, 30, 60, and 90 days).

name: Maize (Corn)
disease_te: కత్తెర పురుగు మరియు ఆకు ఎండు తెగులు
symptoms: Ragged irregular holes on leaves, sawdust-like golden frass inside the central whorl; long boat-shaped greyish-green lesions on leaves.
causes: Spodoptera frugiperda larvae feeding vigorously on whorls; Exserohilum turcicum fungus during moderate temperatures and high humidity.
organic_remedies: Apply neem cake in whorls; release egg parasitoid Telenomus remus; spray Metarhizium anisopliae or Beauveria bassiana @ 5g/L into whorls.
chemical_remedies: Spray Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.5ml/L or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4ml/L directed into central leaf whorl. For blight: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L.
precautions: Early synchronized sowing; intercrop with pulses (cowpea, pigeonpea); avoid staggered sowings in neighboring fields.
suggestions: Place sand mixed with lime/ash in whorls to deter larvae naturally. Inspect early morning when larvae are active.
fertilizer: Apply 100% P and K with 33% N as basal. Remaining N in two splits at knee-high and tasseling stages.

name: Groundnut (Peanut)
disease_te: టిక్కా ఆకుమచ్చ మరియు కాండం కుళ్ళు తెగులు
disease_hi: टिक्का पत्ती धब्बा और कॉलर रॉट
symptoms: Early leaf spot (brown circular spots with prominent yellow halo) and late leaf spot (black circular spots without distinct halo) leading to severe defoliation.
causes: Cercospora arachidicola & Phaeoisariopsis personata fungi spreading rapidly during high humidity and intermittent rains.
organic_remedies: Seed treatment with Trichoderma harzianum @ 10g/kg. Spray 5% neem oil emulsion at first appearance of spots.
chemical_remedies: Spray Hexaconazole 5% EC @ 2ml/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1ml/L or Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP @ 2g/L.
precautions: Crop rotation with non-legumes like sorghum or maize. Avoid water stagnation. Destroy post-harvest haulms.
suggestions: Apply Gypsum @ 200 kg/acre at 40-45 days (pegging stage) to ensure healthy pod filling and disease resistance.
soil_type: Sandy loam, loose porous soil for easy peg penetration, pH 6.0 - 7.0
fertilizer: All N, P, K applied as basal. Top-dress Gypsum at 40-45 days during earthing up.

name: Sugarcane
disease_te: ఎర్ర కుళ్ళు తెగులు మరియు కాటుక తెగులు
symptoms: Third and fourth leaves from top turn yellow and wither. Reddening of internal pith with crosswise white patches and alcoholic fermentation odor.
causes: Colletotrichum falcatum fungus, predominantly seed-borne and spread through infected setts, irrigation water, and soil.
organic_remedies: Hot water sett treatment (52°C for 30 minutes). Sett dipping in Trichoderma viride culture (10g/L).
chemical_remedies: Dip setts in Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L before planting. Spray Carbendazim 1g/L if early symptoms appear in neighboring clumps.
precautions: Use certified disease-free setts; avoid waterlogging; follow 2-year crop rotation; avoid ratooning of infected crop.
suggestions: Rogue out and incinerate infected clumps along with root systems. Use red-rot resistant varieties like Co 0238, Co 86032.
soil_type: Deep rich loamy or clay loam soils with high organic matter, pH 6.5 - 7.5
fertilizer: Basal: 100% P, 25% N, 25% K. Remaining N & K in splits at 45, 90, and 120 days after planting.

name: Banana
disease_hi: पनामा विल्ट और सिगाटोका लीफ स्पॉट
symptoms: Yellowing of lower leaf margins progressing inward, longitudinal splitting of pseudostem base; narrow brown/black streaks on leaves with grey dry centers.
causes: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (soil fungus for Panama); Pseudocercospora fijiensis fungus for Sigatoka during warm rainy periods.
organic_remedies: Soil drenching with Trichoderma viride + Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 20g per plant mixed with 5kg FYM. Spray mineral oil/neem oil for Sigatoka.
chemical_remedies: For Sigatoka: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L + mineral oil 10ml/L. For Panama: Drench Carbendazim 2g/L around the basin (preventive).
precautions: Use tissue-cultured disease-free plantlets (Grand Naine). Provide efficient drainage to prevent waterlogging; avoid moving infected soil.
suggestions: Apply generous quantities of well-rotted organic manure and biofertilizers in planting pits. Maintain potassium supply.
soil_type: Deep well-drained fertile alluvial loam with good moisture retention, pH 6.5 - 7.5
fertilizer: Apply N and K in 5-6 equal splits every 30 days starting from 45 days after planting till flower emergence.

name: Mango
symptoms: Dark brown circular sunken spots on leaves, blossom blight causing flowers to drop, black tear-stain markings on maturing fruits; white powdery coating on inflorescence.
causes: Colletotrichum gloeosporioides (Anthracnose) and Oidium mangiferae (Powdery Mildew), triggered by foggy mornings and sudden rain during flowering.
organic_remedies: Spray wettable sulphur @ 3g/L or Ampelomyces quisqualis bio-fungicide. Spray 5% neem extract at flower bud emergence.
chemical_remedies: First spray at panicle emergence: Wettable Sulphur 80% WDG @ 3g/L. Second spray at fruit set: Azoxystrobin 23% SC @ 1ml/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L.
precautions: Prune dead crisscrossing branches after harvest for sunlight penetration; avoid overhead sprinkling during flowering; collect and destroy fallen leaves.
suggestions: Post-harvest hot water treatment of fruits at 52°C for 10 minutes significantly prevents storage anthracnose.
soil_type: Deep well-drained loamy, alluvial or red soils, pH 5.5 - 7.5
fertilizer: Apply full P, 50% N and 50% K in July-August after harvest; apply remaining N and K in October-November.

name: Paddy (Fine Grain)
disease_te: బాక్టీరియా ఆకు ఎండు తెగులు మరియు పొట్ట కుళ్ళు తెగులు
disease_hi: जीवाणु पत्ती झुलसा और शीथ ब्लाइट
symptoms: Water-soaked translucent stripes along leaf margins turning straw-yellow and wavy. Milky bacterial ooze droplets visible in early morning. Snake-skin like spots on leaf sheath.
causes: Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae bacteria spread through irrigation water, strong winds, and Rhizoctonia solani fungus in dense humid canopies.
organic_remedies: Spray fresh cow dung extract (20g/L) + neem oil (3ml/L). Foliar application of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5g/L.
chemical_remedies: Spray Copper Hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L + Plantomycin / Streptocycline @ 0.1g/L. For sheath blight: Hexaconazole 5% SC @ 2ml/L or Validamycin 3% L @ 2.5ml/L.
precautions: Drain excess water from affected fields for 3-4 days; avoid nitrogen top-dressing when disease is active; maintain 20cm planting row gaps.
suggestions: Avoid field operations during early mornings when dew is present to prevent spreading bacterial ooze on clothing and implements.
soil_type: Clayey loam, fertile river basin soils, pH 6.0 - 7.2
fertilizer: Avoid excess urea. Use Zinc Sulphate 25 kg/ha basal to boost immune defense against bacterial entry.

name: Wheat
disease_te: పసుపు కుంకుమ తెగులు మరియు కాటుక తెగులు
disease_hi: पीला रतुआ (येलो रस्ट) और कन्दुआ रोग
symptoms: Bright yellow pustules arranged in linear stripes on leaves, shedding yellow powdery spores on touch. In loose smut, entire ear turns into black powdery mass.
causes: Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici fungus, favored by cool temperatures (10-15°C) and heavy morning dew.
organic_remedies: Seed solar heat treatment (soak in water for 4 hours then dry in hot sun). Foliar spray of Trichoderma @ 5g/L.
chemical_remedies: At first appearance of yellow rust stripes: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1ml/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1ml/L in 200L water/acre.
precautions: Sow rust-resistant varieties (e.g. HD-2967, HD-3086, DBW-187); sow before Nov 15th to escape peak spore periods; avoid excess irrigation.
suggestions: Monitor northern and sub-mountainous field edges where rust strikes first. Repeat fungicide spray after 15 days if cool humid conditions persist.
soil_type: Fertile, well-drained loams and clay loams, pH 6.0 - 7.5
fertilizer: Apply full P, K and 50% N at sowing. Top dress remaining 50% N at first irrigation (CRI stage) and jointing stage.

name: Brinjal (Eggplant)
disease_te: కొమ్మ మరియు కాయ తొలుచు పురుగు & చిన్న ఆకుల తెగులు
disease_hi: तना एवं फल छेदक और लघु पर्ण रोग
symptoms: Drooping withered tender shoots; circular holes in fruit plugged with excreta; severe reduction in leaf size giving a bushy rosette appearance with no fruiting.
causes: Leucinodes orbonalis larvae boring inside; Little Leaf is a Phytoplasma transmitted by leafhoppers (Hishimonus phycitis).
organic_remedies: Install pheromone traps @ 12/acre (Lucin-lure). Clip and destroy affected shoots weekly. Spray Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or Bt formulations.
chemical_remedies: Spray Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.4ml/L or Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG @ 0.4g/L. For leafhoppers: Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3ml/L.
precautions: Prompt clipping of withered shoots; remove old crop immediately after last harvest; avoid monocropping brinjal.
suggestions: Use barrier crops like coriander or marigold around the field to attract natural parasitic wasps.
soil_type: Rich loamy soil with good drainage, pH 6.0 - 7.0
fertilizer: Basal: 50% N, full P, 50% K. Remaining N and K in two equal splits at 30 and 60 days after transplanting.

name: Okra (Bhindi)
disease: Yellow Vein Mosaic Virus (YVMV) & Powdery Mildew
disease_te: పసుపు ఈనెల తెగులు మరియు బూడిద తెగులు
disease_hi: पीत शिरा मोज़ेक वायरस और चूर्णिल फफूंद
symptoms: Clear yellow network of veins against green leaf tissue, chlorosis, yellow small fruits with reduced market value; white powdery patches on upper leaf surface.
causes: Geminivirus transmitted by whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci); Erysiphe cichoracearum fungus during warm dry days with cool nights.
organic_remedies: Yellow sticky traps @ 15/acre. Spray neem oil (5ml/L) + soap solution. Rogue out infected plants in first 30 days.
chemical_remedies: Control whitefly vector with Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.2g/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L. For powdery mildew: Dinocap 48% EC @ 1ml/L or Wettable Sulphur 3g/L.
precautions: Plant YVMV-tolerant hybrids (e.g. Parbhani Kranti, Arka Anamika); maintain field hygiene; eradicate weed hosts.
suggestions: Spray micronutrient mixture containing zinc and iron at 30 days to improve green foliage retention.
soil_type: Sandy loam to clay loam rich in organic matter, pH 6.0 - 7.5
fertilizer: Apply 50% N, all P and K as basal. Remaining N in 2 splits at 30 and 45 days after sowing.

name: Potato
disease_te: లేట్ బ్లైట్ మరియు బాక్టీరియా వడలు తెగులు
symptoms: Water-soaked irregular green-brown lesions on leaf margins rapidly turning black/purplish, white mildew cottony growth on leaf undersides in morning dew; brown ring in cut tubers.
causes: Phytophthora infestans oomycete, thrives in cold (10-18°C), cloudy, wet and foggy weather conditions.
organic_remedies: Prophylactic spray of Copper Oxychloride @ 2.5g/L. Dip seed tubers in Trichoderma viride culture (10g/L).
chemical_remedies: Prophylactic: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L. Curative: Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2g/L or Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1g/L or Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L.
precautions: Use certified disease-free seed tubers; earth-up properly to protect tubers from fungal wash-off; avoid flood irrigation.
suggestions: Dehaulm (cut top stems) 10-12 days before harvest to prevent tuber infection from dying leaves.
soil_type: Well-aerated sandy loam with loose texture, pH 5.2 - 6.5
fertilizer: Apply 50% N, 100% P and 50% K at planting. Top-dress remaining 50% N and K at earthing up (30-35 days).

name: Pulses (Pigeonpea / Chickpea / Green Gram)
disease_te: ఎండు తెగులు మరియు కాయ తొలుచు పురుగు
symptoms: Drooping and yellowing of foliage from bottom up, dark brown vascular discoloration when main root is split; caterpillar boreholes in pods with chewed seeds.
causes: Fusarium udum / oxysporum soil fungus; Helicoverpa armigera moth larvae laying eggs during flowering.
organic_remedies: Seed treatment with Rhizobium + Trichoderma @ 10g/kg each. Erect bird perches (15/acre). Install pheromone traps @ 5/acre. Spray Helicoverpa NPV (250 LE/acre).
chemical_remedies: For pod borer: Chlorantraniliprole 18.5% SC @ 0.3ml/L or Indoxacarb 14.5% SC @ 0.75ml/L at 50% flowering. For wilt: Carbendazim 2g/L root drenching.
precautions: Deep summer plowing; 3-year crop rotation with sorghum or millets; avoid fields with history of severe Fusarium wilt.
suggestions: Intercropping with sorghum (1:3 or 1:4) acts as a natural barrier against wilt transmission and attracts pest predators.
soil_type: Deep well-drained loamy to black soils, pH 6.5 - 8.0
fertilizer: Basal application of full N, P, K + Sulphur 20 kg/ha. Apply DAP 2% foliar spray at peak flowering to boost pod setting.

name: Coconut
disease: Bud Rot & Rhinoceros Beetle / Red Palm Weevil
disease_te: సుడి కుళ్ళు తెగులు మరియు కొమ్ము పురుగు / ఎర్ర ముక్కు పురుగు
disease_hi: बड रॉट और गैंडा भृंग / लाल ताड़ घुन
symptoms: Yellowing and rotting of innermost spindle leaf with putrid odor; spindle easily pulls out; V-shaped cuts on fronds, fiber extrusion and boreholes in trunk base.
causes: Phytophthora palmivora fungus during continuous heavy rains; Oryctes rhinoceros beetle attacking crowns.
organic_remedies: Clean crown area before monsoon; fill inner leaf axils with mixture of Sevidol 8G (or Neem cake 200g) + sand (200g). Place pheromone traps (Ferrolure+) for weevils.
chemical_remedies: Cut and remove infected spindle tissue, apply Bordeaux paste (10%) or Copper Oxychloride paste (50g in 100ml water) on cut crown surface and protect with polythene cap.
precautions: Ensure good drainage around the palm base; inspect crowns before and during monsoon; avoid wounding trunk tissues.
suggestions: Apply balanced micronutrient mixture (Borax 50g + Magnesium Sulphate 500g) per palm annually to prevent crown deformities.
soil_type: Deep sandy loam, coastal alluvial, or red sandy soil, pH 5.5 - 7.5
fertilizer: Apply in 2 splits: 1/3rd in May-June (pre-monsoon) and 2/3rd in September-October (post-monsoon) along with 50kg green manure/FYM.
